1	# structured/core
2	
3	The row-list editing engine every structured question type builds on:
4	`allergy_intolerance`, `medication_request`, `medication_statement`,
5	`symptom`, `diagnosis`, `appointment`, `encounter`, `service_request`,
6	`charge_item`, `files`, `time_of_death`. 32 files under `structured/types/`
7	import from here (`grep -rl structured/core structured/types`).
8	
9	`structured/` (`registry.ts`, `types.ts`, `pluginRegistry.ts`,
10	`definitions/`) is the registration layer one level up — see the parent
11	`QuestionnaireV2/README.md`'s "structured/" section. **This directory has
12	nothing to do with that registration.** `core` doesn't know
13	`StructuredQuestionType` exists, doesn't know about `registry.ts`, and
14	isn't imported by it. The dependency graph is strictly one-directional:
15	
16	```
17	src/types/questionnaire/structured.ts   (StructuredQuestionType, StructuredEdit — the shipped vocabulary)
18	        │
19	        ▼
20	structured/core/*                       (this directory — generic over TRow, entity-agnostic)
21	        │
22	        ▼
23	structured/types/<entity>/{model.ts,Editor.tsx}   (instantiates core with a concrete TRow)
24	        │
25	        ▼
26	structured/definitions/<entity>.tsx     (glue: component + requires + validate + buildRequests)
27	        │
28	        ▼
29	structured/registry.ts                  (STRUCTURED_TYPE_REGISTRY, resolveStructuredType)
30	```
31	
32	The one crack in that layering: `definitions/appointment.tsx` imports
33	`SINGLETON_ROW_ID` from `core/rowIds.ts` directly, because it builds a
34	translated, row-scoped `QuestionValidationError` at the i18n boundary and
35	needs core's reserved constant to attach a `row_id` to it. Nowhere else in
36	`structured/` or `structured/definitions/` reaches into `core`.
37	
38	Every entity's `model.ts` stays React-free on purpose ("must stay
39	React-free for `node --test`" — a recurring comment across the type
40	modules) and only imports pure core exports (`resolveChanges`, the
41	`BaselineRow`/`ProjectValues`/`SoftDeleteDescriptor` types). Its
42	`Editor.tsx` is the one file that actually calls `useStructuredRows` and
43	renders `StructuredList`. If you're implementing a new structured type,
44	`model.ts` + `Editor.tsx` is the whole job — you should never need to edit
45	anything in this directory.
46	
47	## The data model
48	
49	**A row** is one clinical record (a symptom, a medication, a diagnosis)
50	shaped as a plain object (`TRow extends object` everywhere — nothing here
51	is a class or carries behavior). Its identity is a `RowId` (`type RowId =
52	string`, `types.ts`), minted one of two ways (`rowIds.ts`):
53	
54	- `newRowId()` → `crypto.randomUUID()`, for a row created client-side this
55	  session (add flows on multi-row types).
56	- `SINGLETON_ROW_ID = "singleton"` — a fixed, non-random id for one-row
57	  types (`appointment`, `time_of_death`) that have no server row to key off
58	  until the first save. It's a constant rather than a uuid specifically so
59	  a drafted edit for a singleton still lands on the same identity after a
60	  reload.
61	
62	`RowId` is opaque by design: "nothing parses a rowId; the `op` and the
63	baseline map are what tell add from update" (`rowIds.ts`). Never sniff a
64	rowId's shape to infer whether it's server- or client-issued.
65	
66	**Three shapes, three moments** (`types.ts`):
67	
68	- `BaselineRow<TRow> = { rowId, row }` — one server row, already converted
69	  and keyed by the type module. The hook never fetches and never guesses
70	  ids.
71	- `RowEdit<TRow>` — a `TRow`-parameterized _alias_ of the shipped
72	  `StructuredEdit<TRow>` (`src/types/questionnaire/structured.ts`), not a
73	  restatement: `{ rowId, op: "add"|"update"|"remove", patch: TRow }`.
74	  Aliasing (rather than redeclaring) is what keeps the two from drifting
75	  apart — enforced at compile time by a dedicated erasure-parity test suite
76	  in `deepEqual.test.ts` that pins `EditLog<TRow>` as assignable to
77	  `readonly StructuredEditRecord[]` and asserts a `@ts-expect-error` on an
78	  incomplete `patch`.
79	- `ProjectedRow<TRow> = { rowId, row, origin, edited, softDeleted }` — what
80	  the editor actually renders: baseline merged with any pending edit.
81	  `origin` is `"baseline" | "added"`, and — the one field worth
82	  memorizing — it is **deliberately not derived from `!!row.id`**: a
83	  historical row re-added via `HistoricalRecordSelector` has its id
84	  stripped and is genuinely `"added"` despite having existed before.
85	  `RowStatusSelect`'s `isExistingRecord` prop hinges on getting this
86	  right; its own comment flags `!!row.id` as "the wrong thing to
87	  generalize from."
88	
89	**`EditLog<TRow> = readonly RowEdit<TRow>[]`** is the per-question,
90	at-most-one-entry-per-rowId user-intent log — not append-only, since
91	`applyEditToLog` coalesces a same-rowId edit in place and annihilation
92	splices the entry out entirely — and it's what gets persisted into the
93	response (`response.edits`) and what every `toRequests` reads to build the
94	submit batch.
95	
96	**Invariant, stated three times in three files because it's load-bearing
97	everywhere**: `RowEdit.patch` is always the **complete row**, for every
98	op, including `remove` — never a partial diff, never absent. This is what
99	lets `toRequests` stay pure (no query-cache access needed to reconstruct a
100	row) and lets a draft restored after a failed baseline fetch still carry
101	everything needed to build a soft-delete body. Contrast this with
102	`SoftDeleteDescriptor.patch: Partial<TRow>`, which _is_ allowed to be
103	partial — because it's merged onto an already-known baseline row by
104	`resolveRemoveIntent` (`rowMutations.ts`) — a separate pure function, not
105	the `applyEditToLog` reducer itself — **before** it becomes a `RowEdit`.
106	
107	## The write path: `editLog.ts`
108	
109	`applyEditToLog(log, edit, { baseline?, isEmptyRow? })` is the reducer
110	every mutator funnels through — human clicks and the AI assistant alike
111	call this exact function, which is the actual mechanism (not a code-review
112	convention) that keeps human and assistant edits from diverging. It
113	maintains "at most one entry per rowId" by coalescing the incoming edit
114	against any existing entry for that rowId, per a 12-cell table (existing
115	op `none|add|update|remove` × incoming op `add|update|remove`) documented
116	in the file's header comment. The two facts worth internalizing:
117	
118	- **An op label on an existing entry is not proof of server history.**
119	  Annihilation (`add` → `remove` on a client-only row) erases the rowId's
120	  history from the log entirely. A _later_, unrelated `remove` for that
121	  same rowId then appends fresh (`appendFresh`, unconditional) and can look
122	  baseline-shaped even though the row was never on the server. This is why
123	  resurrection (`remove`/`update` → `add`, or vice versa) is always
124	  resolved against the actual `baseline` map (`resolveOpAgainstBaseline`),
125	  never against what the existing entry's op claims.
126	- **No baseline supplied → conservative fallback to `"update"`.**
127	  `resolveOpAgainstBaseline(rowId, baseline)`: `undefined` baseline always
128	  resolves to `"update"`, because a wrong `update` fails loudly (404/400)
129	  while a wrong `add` would silently duplicate a clinical record — "data
130	  corruption, the worse failure" (comment in `editLog.ts`). This exact
131	  fallback is what the AI assistant's baseline-blind writes rely on (see
132	  below).
133	
134	Collapse-to-pristine (`isRevertedToBaseline`) uses **structural** equality
135	(`deepEqualJson`, `deepEqual.ts`), not `===`, since patches are routinely
136	freshly-constructed objects — a mild→moderate→mild round-trip on an
137	existing baseline row drops the edit from the log entirely.
138	`deepEqualJson` matches `JSON.stringify` semantics (key-order independent,
139	`undefined`-valued keys equated with absent keys, `NaN === NaN`) with two
140	explicit exceptions: array elements compare positionally with **no**
141	undefined-as-absent normalization (arrays are meaningful sequences, not
142	optional-keyed structs), and non-plain objects (`Date`, `Map`, `Set`,
143	`File`, class instances) fall back to reference equality since they
144	aren't JSON-safe to begin with. It does not guard against cycles — every
145	row here is a plain API request object, so a cycle is meant to be a loud
146	caller bug.
147	
148	`dedupeEditsFirstAppearance(log)` is the defensive read-time normalizer:
149	collapses a log to one entry per rowId (last-write-wins on content, first
150	appearance wins on position), for logs that `applyEditToLog` itself would
151	never produce but a restored draft (whose records are validated
152	independently, per-record) might.
153	
154	## The read path: `projectRows.ts`
155	
156	`projectRows(baseline, log, { softDelete?, displayOrder? })` turns
157	"baseline server rows + pending edit log" into what the clinician sees.
158	Order of operations:
159	
160	1. Walk `baseline` in server order; an `op:"remove"` edit hides the row
161	   outright, any other edit replaces its content wholesale (never a field
162	   merge), no edit means the raw baseline row.
163	2. Append `op:"add"` entries from `log`, in log order, after every
164	   baseline row — except an `add` whose rowId step 1 already emitted,
165	   which is skipped: a restored draft can carry an `add` recorded before
166	   the server row existed, and if the fresh baseline now has that id, the
167	   baseline row wins (with the add's patch as its content) rather than one
168	   rowId rendering as two rows.
169	3. **Only when `baseline === undefined`** (loading/errored — not
170	   "confirmed empty"): render unresolved `op:"update"` entries
171	   speculatively as `origin: "baseline"`, so they don't visually flip once
172	   the real baseline resolves. The source is explicit that these are
173	   **unresolved, not orphaned** — "orphan" is reserved for the case where
174	   `baseline` is a known array and the rowId is genuinely missing from it.
175	4. If `displayOrder` is given, stable-sort the output only — never
176	   `baseline` or `log` itself.
177	
178	**The distinction that recurs across this whole module**: `baseline:
179	undefined` means "not yet known"; `baseline: []` means "server confirmed
180	zero rows." Passing `[]` during a real fetch silently drops a restored
181	draft's pending `update` (it gets treated as an orphan) — a dedicated
182	"BASELINE COMPLETENESS CONTRACT" regression test in `projectRows.test.ts`
183	pins exactly this failure mode, and `StructuredRowsOptions.baseline`'s doc
184	comment in `useStructuredRows.ts` states the same rule for callers.
185	
186	Three companion functions consumed only by the hook:
187	
188	- `findOrphanRowIds(baseline, log)` — flags edits whose op isn't `add` and
189	  whose rowId the (confirmed, non-`undefined`) baseline lacks. Notably
190	  does **not** flag the clinician's own `remove` of a row baseline still
191	  has (that's an intentional hard removal, not the row vanishing
192	  server-side) — the subtlety a naive "not in rendered rows" check would
193	  get wrong.
194	- `pruneOrphanEdits(baseline, log)` — drops exactly those rowIds; returns
195	  the same array reference when nothing changed (a reference-equality
196	  escape hatch used by the hook's effect-loop guard, see below).
197	- `truncateToSingletonRow(baseline, log, options)` — enforces mode:
198	  `"single"`'s at-most-one-row invariant by keeping only the first
199	  projected row's rowId. Documented as "closed by construction" — no
200	  shipped singleton type currently exercises the truncating branch, but
201	  encounter's `?toDischarge` seed landing under `SINGLETON_ROW_ID` before
202	  the real (server-id-keyed) baseline resolves is exactly the shape this
203	  guards against.
204	
205	## `changes.ts` — resolving a log into a request batch
206	
207	`resolveChanges(log, { softDelete?, baseline? })` → `{ creates, updates,
208	removes }` is the last stop before each type's own `toRequests` builds
209	wire bodies. It runs the log through `dedupeEditsFirstAppearance`, then
210	for each resolved edit:
211	
212	- Drops (`continue`s past) **orphans** — `op !== "add"` and a supplied
213	  `baseline` map lacks the rowId — silently, from every set. This mirrors
214	  `projectRows`' orphan rule and exists because a `remove` naming a rowId
215	  that never reached the server would, with `softDelete` configured, POST
216	  a soft-delete body to an upsert endpoint and silently **create a
217	  phantom entered-in-error row**.
218	- Reclassifies an `add` whose rowId the baseline already has into an
219	  `update` — the safety net for an edit recorded as `add` while the
220	  baseline query was still in flight (`editLog.ts`'s `coalesceOntoAdd`
221	  never consults baseline, so a later same-rowId edit can leave the entry
222	  looking like an `add` after the baseline resolves). Flagged as "safe for
223	  URL-keyed endpoints (`encounter`, the only reachable case today) but a
224	  `toRequests` for a non-URL-keyed type must re-verify" — the reclassified
225	  row may lack the server `id` a genuine update carries.
226	- Builds a `remove`'s output row, when `softDelete` is configured, as a
227	  **fresh merged object** (`{ ...patch, ...softDelete.patch }`) — never an
228	  alias of either source.
229	
230	Total and pure: never mutates its inputs, always returns fresh arrays
231	(though `creates`/`updates` entries alias the original patch object by
232	reference). When `baseline` is omitted entirely (as opposed to supplied
233	and empty), every edit is trusted — "a documented, conservative fallback,
234	not a guarantee that no orphan reaches the wire."
235	
236	## `rowMutations.ts` — deciding what edit a UI action produces
237	
238	Sits between `StructuredList`'s callbacks and `applyEditToLog`, pulling the
239	branching logic out of the hook into pure, separately-tested functions:
240	
241	- `mergePatch(current, patch, normalizePatch?)` — `{ ...current, ...patch,
242	...normalizePatch?.(current, patch) }`. Three sequential spreads, not a
243	  `??` fallback: `patch` is unconditionally applied in full, and
244	  `normalizePatch`'s result — meant to be derived fields only — lands on
245	  top, adding or overriding but never suppressing the clinician's patch.
246	  A `normalizePatch` that returned something unexpected at a plugin/
247	  `unknown` boundary can only add stray fields on top; it can't erase what
248	  the clinician typed.
249	- `resolveRemoveIntent(entry, softDelete)` — if `entry.origin ===
250	"baseline"` and a `softDelete` descriptor is configured, produces a
251	  soft-delete `update` (marker merged onto current content, row stays
252	  visible/greyed); otherwise a hard `remove`. Gotcha: a row `projectRows`
253	  synthesized speculatively during its step-3 loading window also carries
254	  `origin: "baseline"`, so removing an unconfirmed row records a
255	  soft-delete `update` rather than escalating to a hard delete once the
256	  real baseline lands — tested end-to-end by constructing that exact
257	  loading-window row via `projectRows(undefined, log)` and asserting the
258	  outcome.
259	- `resolveSetRow(input)` — mode:`"single"`'s mutator: `update` against the
260	  existing row if one exists, otherwise `add` under `singletonRowId` built
261	  from `createSeed()`; throws (naming the question id) if neither a
262	  current row nor `createSeed` is available.
263	- `decideInitialEditsSeed(edits, initialEdits)` → `"seed" | "wait" |
264	"skip"`: `edits.length > 0` always wins (`"skip"` — a restored draft
265	  always wins over a seed); no `initialEdits` yet → `"wait"` (**not**
266	  latched — a seed needing the baseline, e.g. encounter's `?toDischarge`,
267	  can legitimately still be `undefined` on first render); otherwise
268	  `"seed"`.
269	
270	## `duplicates.ts` — the add-time dedup guard
271	
272	`findDuplicateCandidates(rows, duplicateKey, candidates)` → one boolean per
273	candidate. No `duplicateKey` configured → always `false` (medication
274	request omits it entirely; clinicians can add the same medication twice on
275	purpose). Otherwise: builds a `seen` set from existing rows'
276	`duplicateKey(row)`, **excluding soft-deleted rows** (re-adding a code
277	previously marked entered-in-error is explicitly allowed), then checks each
278	candidate against `seen`, adding it to `seen` immediately — so two
279	identical candidates in the same batch resolve `[false, true]`, catching
280	same-batch duplicates, not just collisions with pre-existing rows.
281	
282	## `droppedRowsNotice.ts` — labeling what got silently pruned
283	
284	`droppedRowLabels(droppedEdits, rowLabel)` maps the hook's `droppedEdits`
285	(edits `pruneOrphanEdits` removed because their baseline row vanished
286	server-side) into `{ rowId, label }` pairs, falling back to the raw
287	`rowId` when `rowLabel(...)` trims to empty. `rowLabel` is always the
288	_caller's_ responsibility — reusing the same "what does this row mean"
289	logic the editor's `StructuredList` `rowTitle` prop already implements,
290	rather than inventing a second derivation that could drift.
291	
292	## `useStructuredRows` — the hook every editor mounts
293	
294	```ts
295	function useStructuredRows<
296	  TRow extends object,
297	  Mode extends "list" | "single" = "list",
298	>(
299	  options: StructuredRowsOptions<TRow> & { mode?: Mode },
300	): StructuredRowsController<TRow, Mode>;
301	```
302	
303	`StructuredRowsOptions<TRow>`: `questionId`, `baseline?` (see the
304	completeness contract above), `projectValues` (module-scope-stable
305	projection → `ResponseValue[]`; empty projection **must** be `[]` so an
306	emptied section reads as unanswered), `mode?`, `softDelete?`,
307	`duplicateKey?`, `displayOrder?`, `normalizePatch?`, `isEmptyRow?`,
308	`createSeed?`, `singletonRowId?` (defaults `SINGLETON_ROW_ID`),
309	`initialEdits?`, `disabled?`.
310	
311	Return shape is one of two, resolved by a runtime `mode === "single"`
312	check cast into the conditional type — "the one unavoidable seam" between
313	the two:
314	
315	- **`ListRowsController<TRow>`** (default): `rows: ProjectedRow<TRow>[]`,
316	  `addRow`, `addRows`, `updateRow`, `removeRow`, `isDuplicate`.
317	- **`SingleRowController<TRow>`**: `row: ProjectedRow<TRow> | undefined`,
318	  `setRow`, `clearRow`.
319	- Shared base (`StructuredRowsBase<TRow>`): `edits`, `isDirty` (derived,
320	  `edits.length > 0`), `droppedEdits`, `applyEdit` (the raw seam — this is
321	  what the AI assistant would use if it _could_ reach a mounted instance),
322	  `resetEdits` (clears `droppedEdits` too).
323	
324	### Data flow, in order (per render / per effect)
325	
326	1. `[response, updateResponse] = useQuestionResponse(questionId)`, plus
327	   two narrower write paths: `setProjection` (`useSetQuestionProjection`)
328	   and `setRowsPassively` (`useSetQuestionRowsPassively`) — both skip the
329	   "clear this question's showing server errors" side effect that
330	   `updateResponse` always performs, because they're for effects
331	   (background baseline refresh, orphan pruning), not user intent.
332	2. `edits = sanitizeStructuredEditLog(response?.edits)` — the exact same
333	   gate the submit path (`composeStructured.ts`) applies, so display and
334	   submit always start from an identical, well-formed log.
335	3. `rows = projectRows(baseline, edits, {softDelete, displayOrder})`,
336	   computed **synchronously** in `useMemo` — a keystroke paints in the
337	   same render.
338	4. `values = projectValues(rows.map(r => r.row))`, mirrored into the
339	   response by a **separate effect** (`setProjection`, only when
340	   `deepEqualJson(response?.values, values)` is false) — one render behind
341	   `rows`, and deliberately structural rather than ref-based, since a
342	   ref-based guard would either fire a redundant write every commit or
343	   wipe errors on the very first mount.
344	5. **Orphan-prune effect**: early-returns when `orphanRowIds.length === 0`
345	   — explicitly documented as _not_ an optimization but a guard against an
346	   unbounded commit→re-render→commit loop under an unmemoized `baseline`
347	   prop (a fresh-but-still-empty array reference every render would
348	   otherwise retrigger the effect forever). When it does run, it records
349	   the about-to-be-pruned edits into `droppedEdits` **before** calling
350	   `pruneOrphanEdits` (order matters — the prune destroys the only record
351	   of what it removed), and commits via `commitPassively` so `errorsAtom`
352	   is untouched.
353	6. **One-shot `initialEdits` seed**: gated by `decideInitialEditsSeed`,
354	   applied inside `queueMicrotask` behind an `alive` ref armed by its own
355	   effect (not a cleanup flag, which would break under StrictMode's
356	   synchronous mount→cleanup→mount). The deferral exists because React
357	   runs child effects before parent effects on mount, and this hook always
358	   sits below the fill session's dirty-tracking subscription
359	   (`useFillAutosave`) — a synchronous commit would be invisible to that
360	   subscription (no Draft chip, no unsaved-changes prompt).
361	7. Mutators (`applyEdit`, `addRow`/`addRows`, `updateRow`, `removeRow`,
362	   and singleton's `setRow`/`clearRow`) all fold through `applyEditToLog`
363	   and commit via `updateResponse` (real intent, clears shown errors).
364	   `resetEdits` is the one exception: it bypasses `applyEditToLog`
365	   entirely and commits `[]` directly (and clears `droppedEdits`).
366	   `addRows` batches its duplicate check into one `findDuplicateCandidates`
367	   call and skips the commit entirely if every candidate was rejected.
368	
369	**The one documented CAVEAT, worth repeating because it's easy to trip
370	on**: every mutator closes over this render's `edits`. Two mutator calls
371	inside one event handler overwrite each other — the second `commit` wins.
372	`addRows` exists specifically to cover the batch-add case; anything
373	heterogeneous (add one row, remove another, in the same handler) needs
374	manual log-folding through `applyEditToLog` plus one `applyEdit` call.
375	
376	## The UI layer
377	
378	### `StructuredList.tsx` — the shared table/card shell
379	
380	One rendering surface for "a list of editable rows with mobile/desktop
381	parity and shared error semantics," configured (not subclassed) via three
382	exported types:
383	
384	- **`StructuredColumn<TRow>`** — one field definition: `key`, `header`,
385	  `width`, `render(context: StructuredColumnContext<TRow>) => ReactNode`,
386	  plus `required?`, `headerHidden?`, `mobileHidden?`, `ariaLabel?`,
387	  `errorFieldKeys?` (defaults to `[key]` — set this when one column binds
388	  errors across multiple field keys, e.g. `dose_quantity`/`dose_unit`, or
389	  across a variable-length nested array as medication_request's dosage
390	  cells do), `ownsErrorDisplay?` (opt out of the shell's automatic
391	  per-cell `<StructuredFieldError>` when the column renders its own),
392	  `className?`.
393	- **`StructuredColumnContext<TRow>`** — what `render` receives: `row`
394	  (`ProjectedRow<TRow>`), `update: (patch: Partial<TRow>) => void`,
395	  `disabled`, `removed` (mirrors `row.softDeleted`), plus the ARIA/error
396	  bundle (`ariaLabel`, `fieldId`, `describedBy`, `invalid`, `errors`,
397	  `controlProps: StructuredControlProps`). **Gotcha**: `update` is stable
398	  within a render (keyed on `[onUpdateRow, row.rowId]`) but **not** stable
399	  across edits, because `onUpdateRow` (typically `useStructuredRows`'s
400	  `updateRow`) itself changes identity every keystroke — never key a
401	  column's own `useCallback`/`useEffect` on `update`, or you build a
402	  render loop.
403	- **`StructuredRowAction`** — `{ key, label, icon?, onSelect, disabled?,
404	destructive? }` for a row's overflow-menu entries beyond the shell's
405	  built-in Remove (e.g. medication_request/service_request's "Add to
406	  template").
407	
408	Mechanics worth knowing:
409	
410	- **Layout differences are CSS, behavior differences are JavaScript** —
411	  the component contains zero `useBreakpoints` calls; only `lg:`-prefixed
412	  Tailwind classes switch between the desktop `role="table"` grid and the
413	  mobile stacked-card list. The header and every row must render exactly
414	  `columns.length + 1` cells (one spacer for the fixed 48px actions
415	  track) — a column is never skipped from the `.map()`, only its
416	  _content_ is hidden via `headerHidden`/`mobileHidden`, or the shared
417	  `--structured-cols` grid template (from `gridTemplateColumns`,
418	  `structuredListTracks.ts`) misaligns between header and body. The
419	  literal string `lg:grid-cols-[var(--structured-cols)]` must appear
420	  un-templated in both places for Tailwind v4's scanner to emit it.
421	- **A row with a bound blocking error is force-expanded and cannot be
422	  collapsed.** `hasError`/`unmatchedFieldKeys`/`mobileHiddenErrorColumns`
423	  all come from `resolveRowErrorState` (`structuredListRowState.ts`),
424	  which routes every decision through the one shared matcher
425	  (`selectStructuredFieldErrors`, `structuredFieldErrors.ts`), so "has
426	  error," "which keys are unmatched," and "which erroring columns are
427	  mobile-hidden" can never disagree. The mobile card body is
428	  `hidden lg:contents` while collapsed, and that hidden subtree is the
429	  **only** place a cell's `<StructuredFieldError role="alert">` renders —
430	  a blocking error trapped there would never be announced to screen
431	  readers and would silently hard-block Save (`useSubmitFillSession`
432	  aborts on any `QuestionValidationError`). That's why `hasError` disables
433	  the mobile toggle instead of leaving it clickable-but-inert.
434	- **A row-scoped error whose `field_key` no column owns renders nowhere
435	  by default.** This is exactly allergy/symptom/diagnosis's shared `note`
436	  field (`placement: "row"`, no column of its own). `unmatchedFieldKeys`
437	  exists to catch this and render a `lg:col-span-full` fallback block, one
438	  `<StructuredFieldError>` per distinct unmatched key.
439	- A dev-only (`import.meta.env.DEV`) effect, `auditCellAccessibleName`,
440	  walks the committed DOM every render and `console.error`s any
441	  interactive element (matching `INTERACTIVE_SELECTOR`) lacking a real
442	  accessible name — the loud enforcement mechanism for
443	  `StructuredControlProps`, since TypeScript's excess-property checking
444	  does not catch a dropped/misnamed hyphenated ARIA prop.
445	- `rowDisabled` freezes the **entire row div** (`pointer-events-none
446	opacity-40`), including its actions menu — there is currently no way to
447	  freeze fields but still let the clinician act on a disabled row (e.g. a
448	  restore affordance). `canRemoveRow` defaults to `!row.softDeleted`.
449	  Remove is always shell-owned, never something `rowActions` can
450	  override; the separator between custom actions and Remove is inserted
451	  only when both are present.
452	
453	### `AddEntityControl.tsx` and `RowStatusSelect.tsx` — shared leaf primitives
454	
455	Both are used by allergy, symptom, diagnosis, and medication_statement
456	(per their own doc comments); neither imports anything else from `core/`.
457	
458	- **`AddEntityControl<TRow>`** unifies two "add a row from a ValueSet
459	  lookup" flows behind one component: desktop renders `ValueSetSelect` and
460	  commits (`onAdd`) immediately on selection; mobile renders
461	  `EntitySelectionDrawer` and **stages** the created row in local state
462	  (`renderStagedRow` lets the clinician edit it before confirming) —
463	  `open` is _derived_ from `staged !== null`, never independent state, so
464	  "a drawer is open" and "something is staged" can't disagree.
465	- **`RowStatusSelect<TStatus>`** wraps shadcn `Select` for a row's
466	  status/verification dropdown, filtering out exactly one option:
467	  `hiddenForNewRow` is only offered when `isExistingRecord` is true. Its
468	  five ARIA/id props are named key-for-key to spread `{...ctx.controlProps}`
469	  from `StructuredColumnContext` directly onto the real Radix trigger.
470	  `isExistingRecord` must be `row.origin === "baseline"` — not `!!row.id`
471	  — even though they coincide in every current consumer (see the `origin`
472	  gotcha above).
473	
474	### `StructuredDroppedRowsNotice.tsx`
475	
476	Renders a per-question amber `role="alert"` box listing rows dropped this
477	mount (via `droppedRowLabels`), or `null` if `droppedEdits.length === 0` —
478	safe to mount unconditionally in every editor. Deliberately a _separate_
479	mechanism from the pre-Resume `DraftRestoreBar` (mirrors its visual
480	convention on purpose, "reads as one family"): a structured row's drop can
481	only be detected once the question's own baseline refetches, which is
482	always after mount, whereas `DraftRestoreBar` can only name plain answers
483	known at load time.
484	
485	### `StructuredFieldError.tsx` / `structuredFieldErrors.ts`
486	
487	`selectStructuredFieldErrors(errors, { questionId, rowId?, rowIndex?,
488	fieldKeys })` is "the ONE matcher" — every other error-aware piece in this
489	directory (`StructuredList`'s cell wiring, `structuredListRowState.ts`,
490	`StructuredFieldError`) calls it rather than reimplementing matching.
491	Precedence, in order: `question_id` must match; a falsy `field_key`
492	(including `""`, matching `QuestionBlock.tsx`'s own filter) never
493	matches; `fieldKeys.includes(error.field_key)`; then row identity —
494	`error.row_id`, if present, decides the match on its own (even against a
495	coincidentally-matching `index`); else `error.index === rowIndex` (the
496	v1/server index-keyed fallback); else the query itself must be
497	section-level (`rowId === undefined && rowIndex === undefined`). `row_id`
498	strictly outranks `index` — an error carrying both never falls through to
499	index matching, which prevents a stale-index false positive.
500	`StructuredFieldError` renders `<p role="alert">` for the _first_ match
501	only (`error.error || error.msg || t("field_required")`, `||` not `??` —
502	an empty-string message still falls through) and is required reading for
503	why `role="alert"` matters: `QuestionBlock.tsx` filters field-bound errors
504	out of its own block-level list for structured types, so this is the only
505	place those errors get announced.
506	
507	## A simple consumer: `symptom`
508	
509	`model.ts` imports exactly four things from core: `resolveChanges`
510	(`toRequests` builds `[...creates, ...updates,
511	...removes.flatMap(e => e.row ? [e.row] : [])]` from it, no `baseline`
512	passed — trusting every edit is fine here since symptom has no cross-row
513	consistency concerns), and the types `BaselineRow`, `ProjectValues`,
514	`SoftDeleteDescriptor`. `SYMPTOM_SOFT_DELETE` (`{ patch:
515	{verification_status: "entered_in_error"}, isDeleted: row =>
516	row.verification_status === "entered_in_error" }`) is the one constant
517	shared between `toRequests` and the Editor's `useStructuredRows` call.
518	`SymptomRow` **is** `SymptomRequest` — the wire request shape doubles as
519	the row shape; there's no separate editor-only type.
520	
521	`SymptomEditor.tsx` calls `useStructuredRows({ questionId, baseline,
522	projectValues, softDelete: SYMPTOM_SOFT_DELETE, duplicateKey:
523	symptomDuplicateKey, disabled })` — `mode` omitted, so it gets
524	`ListRowsController`. From the return value: `list.rows` → `StructuredList`'s
525	`rows`; `list.updateRow`/`list.removeRow` → `onUpdateRow`/`onRemoveRow`
526	directly, no wrapper; `list.droppedEdits` → `StructuredDroppedRowsNotice`.
527	`addControl` is an `<AddEntityControl<SymptomRow>>` whose `createRow` is
528	`newSymptomRow(code, encounterId)` and whose `onAdd` wraps `list.addRow`
529	to toast on a `"duplicate"` rejection. `list.applyEdit`, `resetEdits`,
530	`edits`, and `isDirty` go entirely unused by this Editor — a good
531	indicator of how much of the hook's surface a "simple" consumer actually
532	touches.
533	
534	## A complex consumer: `medication_request`
535	
536	Contrast: `MedicationRequestEditor` calls `useStructuredRows` with a
537	**smaller** option set than symptom (`questionId`, `baseline`,
538	`projectValues`, `softDelete`, `disabled` — no `duplicateKey`, so
539	`findDuplicateCandidates` always returns `false` and identical medications
540	can be added twice on purpose). The complexity is entirely in
541	columns/render props and surrounding chrome, not hook configuration:
542	
543	- **Per-dosage-instruction columns.** Dose/frequency/duration/instructions
544	  cells set `errorFieldKeys` to arrays from `dosageInstructionFieldKeys`
545	  (`model.ts`), sized by `maxDosageInstructionCount(list.rows)` — the
546	  largest instruction count across all _currently visible_ rows, so
547	  adding an instruction on any row grows every column's key space in the
548	  same render. These columns set `ownsErrorDisplay: true` and render
549	  `<StructuredFieldError>` manually once per instruction index. A shared
550	  `useUpdateInstruction(ctx)` hook wraps `ctx.update` as the single
551	  mutation primitive every instruction-scoped cell routes through, so
552	  "add/remove instruction" and "edit slot N" can't desync on how the
553	  array is rebuilt — and it memoizes on `[ctx.update, ctx.row]`, citing
554	  `StructuredList`'s documented caveat that `ctx.update` isn't stable
555	  across renders.
556	- **`onRemoveRow` is intercepted, not wired straight through** — it sets
557	  `pendingRemoveRowId` and gates the real `list.removeRow` call behind a
558	  confirmation dialog, because an existing row flips to
559	  `entered_in_error` rather than vanishing, and a stray menu click
560	  shouldn't do that silently.
561	- **`rowActions` adds "Add to template"** — exactly the extensibility
562	  point `StructuredRowAction`'s own doc comment names.
563	- **Response templates and historical-record reuse** are _shared_
564	  (`structured/shared/responseTemplates/`), not core — but worth knowing
565	  core doesn't preclude a type from layering substantial extra machinery
566	  on top of the same `useStructuredRows`/`StructuredList` pair.
567	- **`resolveChanges` usage is otherwise identical to symptom's** — same
568	  `{creates, updates, removes}` → flat array pattern in `toRequests`. The
569	  complexity genuinely does not touch the shared engine's contract at
570	  all; it's all in what one column's `render` does with `ctx.update`.
571	
572	The pairing (simplest hook config + most complex UI, vs. richer hook
573	config + simple UI) is the intended shape of this abstraction: `core`
574	carries the row-identity/edit-log/projection bookkeeping uniformly, and
575	each type spends its complexity budget on domain-specific rendering, not
576	on re-deriving row bookkeeping.
577	
578	## How the AI fill-assistant integrates
579	
580	The assistant's `applyStructuredEdit`
581	(`fill/assistant/useFillAssistantSession.ts`) does **not** call
582	`useStructuredRows`. It calls the same two pure primitives the hook's
583	mutators call — `applyEditToLog` (`editLog.ts`) and `projectRows`
584	(`projectRows.ts`) — directly, and writes `responsesAtom` itself via the
585	form store (`store.set`), bypassing `useQuestionResponse`'s setter
586	entirely.
587	
588	This is deliberate, not an oversight, and the reasoning is spelled out in
589	the assistant's own comments: `useStructuredRows` is a **per-question**
590	hook, instantiated only while that question's editor component is
591	mounted, holding that question's fetched `baseline` in its own closure.
592	The assistant's fill-assist handle is built once per fill **session** and
593	must be able to write to a structured question whether or not its editor
594	is currently mounted or scrolled into view — there is no live
595	`useStructuredRows` instance to call into, and no baseline to hand it.
596	
597	Consequences of writing baseline-blind (`applyEditToLog(log, edit, {})`
598	and `projectRows(undefined, log, {})`, both with `baseline: undefined`):
599	
600	- Resurrection ambiguity (`remove`/`update` → `add`) always resolves to
601	  the conservative `"update"` fallback in `resolveOpAgainstBaseline` — the
602	  same designed-in behavior described above, not a special case for the
603	  assistant.
604	- No `isEmptyRow` filtering — that predicate lives in each type's
605	  `model.ts`, "out of this generic handle's reach" — so the assistant's
606	  display mirror can show an all-empty row a mounted editor never would.
607	  Documented as display-only: submit derives from `edits`, not from this
608	  projection.
609	- The assistant replicates `useQuestionResponse`'s error-clearing side
610	  effect by hand (`clearQuestionErrorsInState`) after every write, since
611	  it isn't going through that setter to get it for free.
612	
613	Every write is still gated by `validateStructuredPatch` against the
614	type's own zod `rowSchema` (via `resolveStructuredType` /
615	`rowSchemaOf`, one layer up in `structured/registry.ts` — not part of
616	`core`) — the assistant cannot write a shape core's write path wouldn't
617	otherwise accept.
618	
619	## Invariants and gotchas — read this before touching anything here
620	
621	- **`RowEdit.patch` is always the complete row, every op, including
622	  `remove`.** Never assume it's partial. Never write a `toRequests` or a
623	  UI mutator that constructs a `RowEdit` with anything less than the full
624	  row.
625	- **`baseline: undefined` vs `baseline: []` are never interchangeable.**
626	  `undefined` = not yet resolved; `[]` = server confirmed zero rows.
627	  Getting this backwards (passing `[]` mid-fetch) silently drops a
628	  restored draft's pending edit and is exactly what the "BASELINE
629	  COMPLETENESS CONTRACT" tests in `projectRows.test.ts` guard against.
630	- **`ProjectedRow.origin` is not `!!row.id`.** A stripped-id historical

395	  const alive = useRef(true);
396	  useEffect(() => {
397	    alive.current = true;
398	    return () => {
399	      alive.current = false;
400	    };
401	  });

403	  const seeded = useRef(false);
404	  useEffect(() => {
405	    if (seeded.current) return;
406	    const decision = decideInitialEditsSeed(edits, initialEdits);

408	    seeded.current = true;
409	    if (decision === "skip" || !initialEdits) return;

411	    for (const edit of initialEdits) {
412	      next = applyEditToLog(next, edit, applyOpts);
413	    }
414	    queueMicrotask(() => {

416	    });
417	  }, [initialEdits, edits, applyOpts, commit]);

419	  const applyEdit = useCallback(
420	    (edit: RowEdit<TRow>) => {

423	    },

438	    [rows, duplicateKey],
439	  );
440	
441	  const addRows = useCallback(
442	    (candidates: readonly TRow[]): AddRowResult[] => {
443	      if (disabled) {
444	        return candidates.map(() => ({ ok: false, reason: "disabled" }));
445	      }
446	      const duplicates = findDuplicateCandidates(
447	        rows,
448	        duplicateKey,
449	        candidates,
450	      );
451	      const results: AddRowResult[] = [];
452	      let next = edits;
453	      for (let i = 0; i < candidates.length; i++) {

456	          continue;
457	        }

460	          next,

469	      if (next !== edits) commit(next);

472	    [disabled, rows, duplicateKey, edits, applyOpts, commit],
473	  );

476	    (row: TRow): AddRowResult => addRows([row])[0],

478	  );

482	      if (disabled) return;
483	      const current = rows.find((entry) => entry.rowId === rowId)?.row;
484	      if (!current) return;

490	            op: "update",
491	            patch: mergePatch(current, patch, normalizePatch),
492	          },

495	      );
496	    },
497	    [disabled, rows, normalizePatch, edits, applyOpts, commit],
498	  );
499	
500	  const removeRow = useCallback(
501	    (rowId: RowId) => {
502	      if (disabled) return;
503	      const entry = rows.find((row) => row.rowId === rowId);
504	      if (!entry) return;
505	      commit(
506	        applyEditToLog(
507	          edits,
508	          resolveRemoveIntent(entry, softDelete),
509	          applyOpts,
510	        ),
511	      );
512	    },
513	    [disabled, rows, softDelete, edits, applyOpts, commit],
514	  );
515	
516	  const setRow = useCallback(
517	    (patch: Partial<TRow>) => {

534	      createSeed,

536	      normalizePatch,
537	      questionId,
538	      edits,
539	      applyOpts,
540	      commit,

542	  );

545	    if (disabled) return;
546	    const entry = rows[0];
547	    if (!entry) return;

550	    );
551	  }, [disabled, rows, softDelete, edits, applyOpts, commit]);

553	  const base: StructuredRowsBase<TRow> = {
554	    edits,

562	  // but nothing connects a runtime string comparison to a conditional

567	      row: rows[0],

569	      clearRow,

571	  }
572	  return {
573	    ...base,
574	    rows,
575	    addRow,

577	    updateRow,
578	    removeRow,
579	    isDuplicate,

2	import type {
3	  BaselineRow,
4	  EditLog,
5	  ProjectedRow,
6	  RowEdit,
7	  RowId,
8	  SoftDeleteDescriptor,

11	/**
12	 * Options for {@link projectRows}. Two deliberate narrowings:
13	 *
14	 *  - No `single` flag: a singleton's at-most-one-row invariant is a rowId
15	 *    stability property (`SINGLETON_ROW_ID`), not a truncation this
16	 *    function performs — see {@link truncateToSingletonRow}.
17	 *  - No orphan channel bundled into the return: {@link findOrphanRowIds}
18	 *    is the sibling function over the same `(baseline, log)` inputs.
19	 *
20	 * `baseline` is the COMPLETE fetched server-row set, or `undefined` while
21	 * unknown — never a partial array standing in for "loading".
22	 */
23	export interface ProjectRowsOptions<TRow extends object> {
24	  /**
25	   * How a type marks — instead of deletes — a baseline row's removal.
26	   * See `SoftDeleteDescriptor` in `./types` for the full contract.
27	   *
28	   * Read here only via `isDeleted`, to decide `ProjectedRow.softDeleted`
29	   * for whatever row content is already on screen — a row can be flagged
30	   * because its baseline data already carries the marker (soft-deleted in
31	   * an earlier session) just as much as because this session's edit added
32	   * it. `projectRows` never writes the marker itself; that is
33	   * `removeRow`'s job.
34	   */
35	  softDelete?: SoftDeleteDescriptor<TRow>;
36	  /**
37	   * DISPLAY ONLY. Applied as a stable sort over the canonical order
38	   * (baseline order, then added rows in edit-log order). Nothing
39	   * downstream reads row order — requests are built from the edit log,
40	   * identity from `rowId` — so this sort can never reach the edit log, a
41	   * request body, or a rowId.
42	   */
43	  displayOrder?: (a: TRow, b: TRow) => number;
44	}
45	
46	/**
47	 * Computes what the clinician SEES for one structured section: baseline
48	 * (complete fetched server-row set, or `undefined` while unknown) plus
49	 * the pending edit log. This is what `values[0].value` carries for every
50	 * v2 structured question — the answered predicate, outline ticks,
51	 * readonly renderers and server-draft dumps all read the array this
52	 * returns. Pure: never mutates `baseline` or `log`.
53	 *
54	 * Steps, in order:
55	 *
56	 * 1. Baseline rows, in the order the query layer returned them — a row's
57	 *    position never depends on whether it was edited. An `op: "remove"`
58	 *    edit hides the row outright (a marking type's `removeRow` records an
59	 *    `update`, never a `remove`, so this branch is a genuine delete). Any
60	 *    other matching edit contributes `edit.patch` as the row's content —
61	 *    a full REPLACE, never a merge: `patch` is always the complete row.
62	 *
63	 * 2. Added rows, in edit-log order — stable across a baseline refetch. An
64	 *    `add` whose rowId step 1 already emitted is SKIPPED: a restored
65	 *    draft can carry an `add` recorded before the server row existed
66	 *    while the fresh baseline now has that id — the baseline row wins,
67	 *    with the add's patch as its content, rather than one rowId rendering
68	 *    as two rows.
69	 *
70	 * 3. When `baseline` is a known array, every remaining `update`/`remove`
71	 *    is an orphan — intent about a row the complete baseline lacks — and
72	 *    is never rendered; {@link findOrphanRowIds} names these. When
73	 *    `baseline` is `undefined` (loading/errored), an unmatched `update`
74	 *    is unresolved, not orphaned — see step 3 in the implementation.
75	 *
76	 * 4. `displayOrder`, applied last via a stable sort.
77	 */
78	export function projectRows<TRow extends object>(
79	  baseline: readonly BaselineRow<TRow>[] | undefined,
80	  log: EditLog<TRow>,
81	  options: ProjectRowsOptions<TRow> = {},
82	): ProjectedRow<TRow>[] {
83	  const { softDelete, displayOrder } = options;
84	
85	  const editByRowId = new Map<RowId, RowEdit<TRow>>();
86	  for (const edit of log) editByRowId.set(edit.rowId, edit);
87	
88	  // `undefined` means "not yet known"; only the ORIGINAL `baseline`
89	  // parameter is what step 3 branches on.
90	  const baselineRows = baseline ?? [];
91	  const baselineRowIds = new Set<RowId>(
92	    baselineRows.map((entry) => entry.rowId),
93	  );
94	
95	  const rows: ProjectedRow<TRow>[] = [];
96	
97	  // 1. Baseline, in the order the query layer returned it.
98	  for (const entry of baselineRows) {
99	    const edit = editByRowId.get(entry.rowId);
100	    if (edit?.op === "remove") continue;
101	
102	    const row = edit ? edit.patch : entry.row;
103	
104	    rows.push({
105	      rowId: entry.rowId,
106	      row,
107	      origin: "baseline",
108	      edited: edit !== undefined,
109	      softDeleted: softDelete?.isDeleted(row) ?? false,
110	    });
111	  }
112	
113	  // 2. Adds, in edit-log order. Two guards:
114	  //    - `editByRowId.get(edit.rowId) !== edit` skips an entry a later
115	  //      entry for the same rowId superseded (`applyEditToLog` never
116	  //      produces duplicates, but a restored draft's per-record
117	  //      validation admits them).
118	  //    - `baselineRowIds.has(edit.rowId)` skips a rowId loop 1 already
119	  //      emitted — see the collision note in the doc comment.
120	  for (const edit of log) {
121	    if (editByRowId.get(edit.rowId) !== edit) continue;
122	    if (edit.op !== "add") continue;
123	    if (baselineRowIds.has(edit.rowId)) continue;
124	
125	    rows.push({
126	      rowId: edit.rowId,
127	      row: edit.patch,
128	      origin: "added",
129	      edited: true,
130	      softDeleted: softDelete?.isDeleted(edit.patch) ?? false,
131	    });
132	  }
133	
134	  // 3. `baseline === undefined` means the query is loading or errored,
135	  //    NOT "the server confirmed zero rows" — an unmatched `update` is
136	  //    unresolved, not a confirmed orphan. Render it from its own patch
137	  //    (already the complete row) so a restored draft stays visible — and
138	  //    still submittable — during the loading window. `origin` is
139	  //    "baseline" so the row doesn't visually flip when the real baseline
140	  //    arrives and confirms it.
141	  if (baseline === undefined) {
142	    for (const edit of log) {
143	      if (editByRowId.get(edit.rowId) !== edit) continue;
144	      if (edit.op !== "update") continue;
145	
146	      rows.push({
147	        rowId: edit.rowId,
148	        row: edit.patch,
149	        origin: "baseline",
150	        edited: true,
151	        softDeleted: softDelete?.isDeleted(edit.patch) ?? false,
152	      });
153	    }
154	  }
155	
156	  // 4. Display sort — output only.
157	  if (displayOrder) {
158	    rows.sort((a, b) => displayOrder(a.row, b.row));
159	  }
160	
161	  return rows;
162	}

164	/**
165	 * Names the rowIds {@link projectRows} silently drops: a restored edit
166	 * whose baseline row vanished server-side must be LISTED to the
167	 * clinician, not just disappear. Computed over the identical
168	 * `(baseline, log)` inputs `projectRows` takes, so the two can never
169	 * disagree about which edits are showing versus orphaned.
170	 *
171	 * `undefined` baseline returns `[]`: unresolved is not confirmed-gone.
172	 *
173	 * The predicate is `op !== "add" && !baselineRowIds.has(rowId)` —
174	 * deliberately NOT "not rendered", which would also flag the clinician's
175	 * own remove of an added row and every ordinary `add`.
176	 *
177	 * Pure; duplicates in a malformed log are reported once
178	 * ({@link dedupeEditsFirstAppearance}).
179	 */
180	export function findOrphanRowIds<TRow extends object>(
181	  baseline: readonly BaselineRow<TRow>[] | undefined,
182	  log: EditLog<TRow>,
183	): readonly RowId[] {
184	  if (baseline === undefined) return [];
185	  const baselineRowIds = new Set<RowId>(baseline.map((entry) => entry.rowId));
186	
187	  const orphanRowIds: RowId[] = [];
188	  for (const edit of dedupeEditsFirstAppearance(log)) {
189	    if (edit.op !== "add" && !baselineRowIds.has(edit.rowId)) {
190	      orphanRowIds.push(edit.rowId);
191	    }
192	  }
193	  return orphanRowIds;
194	}
195	
196	/**
197	 * Drops every {@link findOrphanRowIds} entry from `log`: what remains is
198	 * exactly what `projectRows` still renders (plus what it presumes during
199	 * the loading window) — never intent about a row the complete, known
200	 * baseline has confirmed gone.
201	 *
202	 * This lives at the hook, not the compose/submit seam: `toRequests` and
203	 * `resolveChanges` never hold a baseline at submit time, so
204	 * `useStructuredRows` — the one place `baseline` and `edits` coexist —
205	 * must prune before its `commit` write.
206	 *
207	 * Deliberately NOT the clinician's `removeRow` path: no soft-delete
208	 * marker is written and no request is implied — the entry is simply
209	 * excised. A no-op while `baseline` is `undefined`.
210	 *
211	 * Pure; returns the SAME `log` reference when nothing is dropped, so a
212	 * caller can skip a write on reference equality.
213	 */
214	export function pruneOrphanEdits<TRow extends object>(
215	  baseline: readonly BaselineRow<TRow>[] | undefined,
216	  log: EditLog<TRow>,
217	): EditLog<TRow> {
218	  const orphanRowIds = findOrphanRowIds(baseline, log);
219	  if (orphanRowIds.length === 0) return log;
220	  const orphanSet = new Set(orphanRowIds);
221	  return log.filter((edit) => !orphanSet.has(edit.rowId));
222	}
223	
224	/**
225	 * Restricts an edit log to at most the ONE rowId {@link projectRows}
226	 * would show as `rows[0]` for the same `(baseline, log)` pair.
227	 *
228	 * Why: singleton mode only ever SHOWS `rows[0]`, but nothing upstream
229	 * stops the log from holding a second rowId — an `initialEdits` seed
230	 * writes an `add` under `singletonRowId`, an `add` is never an orphan,
231	 * and if a real baseline row for the same question resolves under its
232	 * OWN server id while that seed is still in the log, the two coexist: a
233	 * caller writing `edits` from every projected row would silently submit
234	 * BOTH on Save. Keeps whichever rowId `projectRows` shows FIRST, so "the
235	 * one row" is defined by the exact projection the clinician sees.
236	 *
237	 * Unreachable for every type shipped so far — closed by construction
238	 * rather than left as a trap for the next singleton.
239	 *
240	 * Pure; returns the SAME `log` reference when there is nothing to drop.
241	 */
242	export function truncateToSingletonRow<TRow extends object>(
243	  baseline: readonly BaselineRow<TRow>[] | undefined,
244	  log: EditLog<TRow>,
245	  options: ProjectRowsOptions<TRow> = {},
246	): EditLog<TRow> {
247	  if (log.length === 0) return log;
248	  // Checks the FULL PROJECTION's row count, not `log.length` — a baseline
249	  // can contribute rows the log never mentions (a real baseline row under
250	  // its own id, plus a single seeded `add` under a different id, is a
251	  // one-entry log that still projects TWO rows).
252	  const rows = projectRows(baseline, log, options);
253	  if (rows.length <= 1) return log;
254	  const keepRowId = rows[0]?.rowId;
255	  // No row projects at all — nothing to keep; leave `log` for orphan
256	  // pruning to handle. Defensive: unreachable alongside `rows.length > 1`.
257	  if (keepRowId === undefined) return log;
258	  const truncated = log.filter((edit) => edit.rowId === keepRowId);
259	  return truncated.length === log.length ? log : truncated;
260	}

3	 * the `StructuredQuestionType` union derives from. Lives in the types layer
4	 * so `src/types/*` never imports from the components tree.
5	 *
6	 * Adding a type here is step one of the checklist in
7	 * `src/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/` — the total registry there
8	 * refuses to compile until the new member has a definition.
9	 */
10	export const STRUCTURED_QUESTION_TYPES = [
11	  "allergy_intolerance",
12	  "medication_request",
13	  "medication_statement",
14	  "symptom",
15	  "diagnosis",
16	  "encounter",
17	  "time_of_death",
18	  "files",
19	  "service_request",
20	  "charge_item",
21	  "appointment",
22	] as const;
23	
24	export type StructuredQuestionType = (typeof STRUCTURED_QUESTION_TYPES)[number];
25	
26	/**
27	 * A structured type contributed at runtime by a federation plugin. Always
28	 * namespaced `{plugin_slug}.{type_name}` — bare names stay reserved for
29	 * core, so a plugin can never shadow a built-in type. The template literal
30	 * documents the shape to the type system; the real gate is
31	 * `PLUGIN_STRUCTURED_TYPE_PATTERN` below (TS cannot express the character
32	 * class), enforced at registration and by `isPluginStructuredTypeName`.
33	 */
34	export type PluginStructuredTypeName = `${string}.${string}`;
35	
36	/** The one definition of a well-formed plugin type id. Both the registry's
37	 *  throw-on-register check and the `isPluginStructuredTypeName` guard read
38	 *  it, so there is a single source for the rule. */
39	export const PLUGIN_STRUCTURED_TYPE_PATTERN = /^[a-z0-9_]+\.[a-z0-9_]+$/;
40	
41	/**
42	 * What a `structured_type` field may hold: a core type or a plugin one.
43	 * Keeping the core union as a member means a `switch`/`===` on a core
44	 * literal still narrows — the template-literal member never swallows it.
45	 */
46	export type StructuredTypeValue =
47	  StructuredQuestionType | PluginStructuredTypeName;
48	
49	/** Narrows a `structured_type` back to a core member — the guard anything
50	 *  keyed on the closed core union (a total `Record`, a core-only handler
51	 *  map) needs now that the field also admits plugin ids. */
52	export function isCoreStructuredType(
53	  value: string,
54	): value is StructuredQuestionType {
55	  return (STRUCTURED_QUESTION_TYPES as readonly string[]).includes(value);
56	}
57	
58	/** Narrows a registered plugin type's id to `PluginStructuredTypeName` —
59	 *  what a consumer holding the definition's `string` `type` needs to put it
60	 *  where a `StructuredTypeValue` is expected, without a cast. */
61	export function isPluginStructuredTypeName(
62	  value: string,
63	): value is PluginStructuredTypeName {
64	  return PLUGIN_STRUCTURED_TYPE_PATTERN.test(value);
65	}
66	
67	/**
68	 * Clinician changes to a structured section, distinct from projection display
69	 * state. `rowId` is stable and client-owned: the server id for existing rows,
70	 * or a uuid for new rows. `patch` is the complete row for every operation so
71	 * request composition remains self-sufficient.
72	 */
73	export type StructuredEditOp = "add" | "update" | "remove";
74	
75	export interface StructuredEdit<TRow> {
76	  /** Server id for a row that exists on the server; uuid for an add. */
77	  rowId: string;
78	  op: StructuredEditOp;
79	  patch: TRow;
80	}
81	
82	/**
83	 * The type-erased edit, as it is stored on a `QuestionnaireResponse`, in a
84	 * local draft and in a server draft's `response_dump`. A row shape is
85	 * opaque outside its own type module — the same honesty `unknown[]` buys
86	 * `ResolvedStructuredType`'s data reads — so `patch` widens to `unknown`
87	 * and the ONE sanctioned narrowing back happens at the registry boundary,
88	 * where key-correlation already guarantees the pairing.
89	 */
90	export type StructuredEditRecord = StructuredEdit<unknown>;
91	
92	const STRUCTURED_EDIT_OPS: readonly string[] = ["add", "update", "remove"];
93	
94	/** Is this parsed-JSON value a well-formed edit? Drafts and server dumps are
95	 *  untrusted blobs, and this guard is the ONLY gate one passes before
96	 *  `useStructuredRows` casts the sanitized log to `EditLog<TRow>`.
97	 *
98	 *  `patch` is checked for PRESENCE only — a non-null object — because it is
99	 *  the complete row for every op (see {@link StructuredEdit}) and the first
100	 *  thing every reader dereferences (`softDelete.isDeleted`, `duplicateKey`,
101	 *  an editor's `rowTitle`); a truncated `{ rowId, op }` entry would throw
102	 *  out of render and take the whole fill page with it. Its CONTENTS stay
103	 *  unjudged here — only the type's own row schema can rule on those, and
104	 *  request building has its own containment boundary. */
105	export function isStructuredEditRecord(
106	  value: unknown,
107	): value is StructuredEditRecord {
108	  if (typeof value !== "object" || value === null) return false;
109	  const candidate = value as { rowId?: unknown; op?: unknown; patch?: unknown };
110	  return (
111	    typeof candidate.rowId === "string" &&
112	    candidate.rowId.length > 0 &&
113	    typeof candidate.op === "string" &&
114	    STRUCTURED_EDIT_OPS.includes(candidate.op) &&
115	    typeof candidate.patch === "object" &&
116	    candidate.patch !== null
117	  );
118	}
119	
120	/**
121	 * Sanitizes an untrusted edit log: drops malformed entries and collapses
122	 * duplicate `rowId`s to the last entry's content while preserving the first
123	 * entry's position. Map insertion order keeps the surviving entry at that
124	 * first position when an existing key is updated.
125	 */
126	export function sanitizeStructuredEditLog(
127	  raw: unknown,
128	): StructuredEditRecord[] {
129	  if (!Array.isArray(raw)) return [];
130	  const byRowId = new Map<string, StructuredEditRecord>();
131	  for (const entry of raw) {
132	    if (!isStructuredEditRecord(entry)) continue;
133	    byRowId.set(entry.rowId, entry);
134	  }
135	  return [...byRowId.values()];
136	}

content.text:
Review complete — 13 agents swept the module (inventory, usage census, requirements trace, boilerplate analysis, test-leverage audit, then a simplifier vs. defender debate with adversarial verification of every deletion claim). Here's the verdict.

## Bottom line

**The center of the abstraction earns its complexity. Roughly 15–20% of it doesn't.** The honest simplification is not a rewrite — it's a subtraction: ~600–800 production lines plus ~1,000 test lines of consumer-less fringe can go today, one convention should become a type, and the boilerplate you're actually feeling lives *above* core, not inside it.

## Why the center is essential, not ceremony

The whole design hangs off one decision: persisting clinician intent as an edit log (`response.edits`) rather than a rows snapshot. That decision is forced by a shipped, E2E-exercised requirement — **draft restore**. [fillDraftCore.ts:82](src/components/QuestionnaireV2/fill/draft/fillDraftCore.ts:82) persists `edits` and strips `values`; a restored draft must render and remain submittable *before* the baseline query resolves, and a submit-time diff can't distinguish "remove this server row" from "never touched it" across a reload. The evaluated alternative (per-editor local state + diff-at-submit) fails that requirement outright, and the boilerplate analysis found bespoke rewrites come out **longer** for 8 of 11 types — chargeItem proves the marginal cost floor is ~30–50 wiring lines per type, with ~2,800 core lines amortized 11 ways.

The test suite has real leverage too, which surprised me for a 4-day-old module: the verifiers confirmed the legacy v1 bugs the tests cite by reading the deleted v1 source (diagnosis lists silently reordered on write-back, appointment rows annihilated when emptied), and commit af9f5eafc pinned four timezone bugs that were live but green-in-UTC. The hook's three gnarliest pieces (microtask-deferred seed, orphan-prune guard, StrictMode-safe latch) each trace to an observed bug, not speculation.

## What's verifiably deletable (each claim adversarially verified)

| Claim | Verdict | What goes |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | CONFIRMED | Dead controller/API surface: `applyEdit`, `resetEdits`, `edits`, `isDirty`, `isDuplicate`, `singletonRowId`, `removeLabel`, `canRemoveRow`, `StructuredColumn.className`, `ctx.removed` — zero production consumers. `applyEdit`'s doc comment cites an assistant integration that provably bypasses the hook ([useFillAssistantSession.ts:23](src/components/QuestionnaireV2/fill/assistant/useFillAssistantSession.ts:23) imports the pure functions directly). ~70–90 LOC. |
| S2 | CONFIRMED | `resolveChanges`' `baseline` param, orphan-drop, and add→update reclassification — **no caller ever passes a populated baseline**; the README's claim that encounter is the reachable case is wrong (it passes `{}`). Structurally unreachable, ~230 LOC with tests. |
| S3 | PARTIAL | `truncateToSingletonRow`'s truncating branch — unreachable for all 3 singleton types; replace with a dev-mode assertion (the guarded failure is double-submit of clinical data, so assert rather than bare-delete). ~140 LOC net. |
| S4 | PARTIAL | Downstream duplicate-rowId defense-in-depth — the dedup *already* lives in `sanitizeStructuredEditLog`; the three downstream copies are deletable, ~25–30 LOC + ~250 test LOC. |
| S5 | CONFIRMED | The `error.index` fallback and `rowIndex` plumbing in error matching — zero producers repo-wide; server errors are question-level only ([mapBatchErrors.ts:69](src/components/QuestionnaireV2/fill/submit/mapBatchErrors.ts:69)), every row-keyed error is client-made with `row_id`. |
| S6 | PARTIAL | The `mode: "single"` conditional-return-type cast — keep the internal branch, expose two typed wrapper hooks instead; kills the inference trap documented four separate times. Net ~0–30 LOC but real ergonomic win. |

## The three bigger calls (yours to make, not verified deletions)

1. **`fill/assistant` is the largest consumer-less mass: 3,164 lines, fully built and unit-tested, with zero invocable consumer** — `REACT_ENABLED_APPS` is empty, no plugin registers a form assistant, the window test bridge has no spec using it. It's also the only justification for `applyEditToLog`'s baseline-blind fallback. If the scribe plugin is imminent, keep it; if it's a someday, this is the single biggest deletion available, and git history preserves it.

2. **The `undefined`-vs-`[]` baseline convention should be a discriminated union.** It's the module's self-identified most dangerous contract, enforced today only by prose — doc comments, five `NO_BASELINE` constants with justification blocks, and a dedicated regression suite. The natural TanStack idiom (`data?.results ?? []`) produces exactly the failure mode. Making it `{status: "loading"} | {status: "loaded", rows}` retires the hazard and a large slice of the ~1,700 lines of comment/README burden — which is really the tax you're feeling when you read this module.

3. **The boilerplate in the type modules points at a missing mid-layer, not at core being too fat.** Symptom/diagnosis/allergy/medicationStatement are near-clones (their staged mobile forms differ by 37 normalized diff lines); ~700–900 lines would collapse under a field-descriptor layer that renders the desktop column and mobile staged field from one definition. Meanwhile the genuinely over-engineered corner is `mode: "single"` for *create-only* singletons — timeOfDeath is ~92 lines where bespoke would be ~35, pure protocol compliance for one datetime field.

## One caveat on "shipped"

Everything above rates requirements against this branch — QuestionnaireV2 exists only on `bodhi/questionnaire-fill` (226 commits ahead of develop), so "shipped-and-exercised" means wired into reachable routes with E2E coverage, not production-proven. The requirements trace also flagged that symptom's baseline query uses `limit: 100`, which technically violates the baseline-completeness contract the orphan pruner depends on — worth a look regardless of what else you do.

The full evidence (per-mechanism inventory, complete usage census, per-claim verification reasoning) is in the workflow output if you want to drill in. If you want, I can turn S1–S6 into a cleanup PR — they're all verified safe against the pinned tests and E2E suite.

29	 */

31	  /** New rows, in log order. An `add` edit's `patch` already IS the

41	   */

48	  /** How this type marks — instead of deletes — a row's removal. See
49	   *  `SoftDeleteDescriptor`'s doc comment (`./types`) for the full

51	   *  is none) rather than defaulted, so a type module's differ makes the
52	   *  "does this type soft-delete?" call on purpose at every call site,
53	   *  not by omission. */
54	  softDelete?: SoftDeleteDescriptor<TRow>;
55	  /**
56	   * rowId → the unedited server row: the COMPLETE fetched server-row set,
57	   * or `undefined` while it is unknown (loading/errored) — never a
58	   * partial map.
59	   *
60	   * When supplied, an `update`/`remove` whose `rowId` it lacks is an
61	   * orphan — intent about a row the server no longer has (typically a
62	   * restored draft), or a `remove` for a rowId that never reached the
63	   * server. Orphans are dropped entirely, matching `projectRows`' orphan
64	   * rule; an `add` is never an orphan. When `undefined`, every edit is
65	   * trusted and dispatched — a documented, conservative fallback, not a
66	   * guarantee that no orphan reaches the wire.
67	   */
68	  baseline?: ReadonlyMap<RowId, TRow>;

71	/**
72	 * Resolves one edit log into the create/update/remove sets a type's
73	 * `toRequests(edits, ctx)` sends over the wire. An empty log yields three
74	 * empty arrays regardless of `baseline` — a clinician who never touched a
75	 * section sends zero requests for it, by construction.
76	 *
77	 * Pure and total: never mutates `log` or `options`; always returns fresh
78	 * arrays.
79	 *
80	 * Op semantics stop here: this realizes the log's add/update/remove
81	 * INTENT; whether a given wire call actually creates or updates
82	 * server-side is each type's `toRequests` contract (the real endpoints
83	 * are upserts that may create instead of failing on an unrecognized id).

86	 * but admitted by a restored draft's per-record validation) is
87	 * de-duplicated last-write-wins per rowId and dispatched once, at first
88	 * appearance — otherwise `[add("dup", a), add("dup", b)]` would dispatch
89	 * two creates for one identity.
90	 *
91	 * An `add` whose rowId `baseline` already contains is reclassified into
92	 * `updates`: the reducer keeps `op: "add"` for edits recorded while the
93	 * baseline query was still loading, and emitting a create for a row the
94	 * server already has would silently duplicate a clinical record. The
95	 * reclassified row is the add's `patch` verbatim — see
96	 * {@link ResolvedChanges.updates} for why it may lack a server `id`.
97	 *
98	 * A `remove` can name a rowId that never reached the server (add→remove
99	 * annihilates the pair and erases its history; a second remove then
100	 * appends fresh). With `softDelete` configured, trusting that op would
101	 * POST a soft-delete body to an upsert endpoint that CREATES a phantom
102	 * row already marked entered-in-error — hence the orphan check against
103	 * `baseline`; see {@link ResolveChangesOptions.baseline}.
104	 */
105	export function resolveChanges<TRow extends object>(
106	  log: EditLog<TRow>,
107	  options: ResolveChangesOptions<TRow>,
108	): ResolvedChanges<TRow> {
109	  const { softDelete, baseline } = options;
110	
111	  const creates: TRow[] = [];
112	  const updates: TRow[] = [];
113	  const removes: ResolvedRemove<TRow>[] = [];
114	
115	  for (const resolved of dedupeEditsFirstAppearance(log)) {
116	    const isOrphan =
117	      resolved.op !== "add" &&
118	      baseline !== undefined &&
119	      !baseline.has(resolved.rowId);
120	    if (isOrphan) continue; // see ResolveChangesOptions.baseline's doc comment
121	
122	    switch (resolved.op) {
123	      case "add":
124	        // Baseline already has this rowId — creating it again would
125	        // duplicate a server row, so it dispatches as an update.
126	        (baseline?.has(resolved.rowId) ? updates : creates).push(
127	          resolved.patch,
128	        );
129	        break;
130	      case "update":
131	        updates.push(resolved.patch);
132	        break;
133	      case "remove":
134	        removes.push(
135	          softDelete
136	            ? {
137	                rowId: resolved.rowId,
138	                row: { ...resolved.patch, ...softDelete.patch },
139	              }
140	            : { rowId: resolved.rowId },
141	        );
142	        break;
143	      // No default: an unrecognized op (reachable only via a cast — draft
144	      // validation rejects unknown op strings) is deliberately dropped
145	      // from every set. An op outside the closed vocabulary says nothing
146	      // this function can act on.
147	    }
148	  }
149	
150	  return { creates, updates, removes };
151	}

 * Passes an explicit, KNOWN-EMPTY `baseline` — not `{}` (baseline

function resolveSingletonRow(
  edits: readonly StructuredEdit<AppointmentRow>[],
): AppointmentRow | undefined {
  const { creates } = resolveChanges(edits, { baseline: new Map() });
  return creates[0];
}

23	/** Does any error bind to this column's cell in this row? The same matcher

25	function columnHasBoundError(

41	 *  defaulting to `[column.key]`) — the set a fallback slot must NOT
42	 *  duplicate. */
43	function knownFieldKeys(columns: readonly ErrorProneColumn[]): Set<string> {
44	  return new Set(
45	    columns.flatMap((column) => column.errorFieldKeys ?? [column.key]),
46	  );
47	}

49	/**
50	 * Distinct `field_key`s, bound to THIS row, that belong to no declared
51	 * column.
52	 *
53	 * A row-scoped error whose `field_key` no column owns would otherwise
54	 * render NOWHERE: per-cell checks key on `column.errorFieldKeys ??
55	 * [column.key]`, and `QuestionBlock`'s allow-list suppresses the same
56	 * error from the block-level list — message deleted from the page,
57	 * `role="alert"` never rendered, row still collapsible, Save
58	 * hard-blocked with no visible reason. This names those keys so a
59	 * fallback slot can render them and {@link resolveRowErrorState}'s
60	 * `hasError` can force the row open.
61	 *
62	 * Reuses `selectStructuredFieldErrors` (the same matcher every per-cell
63	 * check uses) to CONFIRM each candidate is actually bound to this
64	 * row/question — the candidate scan only narrows which keys to ask
65	 * about; it never re-implements row-identity matching, so this cannot
66	 * drift from the per-cell checks.

68	export function unmatchedRowErrorFieldKeys(
69	  columns: readonly ErrorProneColumn[],
70	  errors: readonly QuestionValidationError[],
71	  match: RowErrorMatch,
72	): string[] {
73	  const known = knownFieldKeys(columns);
74	  const candidates = Array.from(
75	    new Set(
76	      errors
77	        .map((error) => error.field_key)
78	        .filter(
79	          (fieldKey): fieldKey is string =>
80	            fieldKey !== undefined && !known.has(fieldKey),
81	        ),
82	    ),
83	  );
84	  return candidates.filter(
85	    (fieldKey) =>
86	      selectStructuredFieldErrors(errors, {
87	        questionId: match.questionId,
88	        rowId: match.rowId,
89	        rowIndex: match.rowIndex,
90	        fieldKeys: [fieldKey],
91	      }).length > 0,
92	  );

99	 *  disagree with each other. */

103	  hasError: boolean;

106	  unmatchedFieldKeys: string[];
107	  /** Columns carrying an error whose cell is `display:none` below `lg`.

109	   *  row would pin itself open, disable its own collapse toggle and block
110	   *  Save while showing nothing — the caller re-renders these in a slot
111	   *  that is visible there. */
112	  mobileHiddenErrorColumns: TColumn[];

115	export function resolveRowErrorState<TColumn extends ErrorProneColumn>(
116	  columns: readonly TColumn[],
117	  errors: readonly QuestionValidationError[],
118	  match: RowErrorMatch,
119	): RowErrorState<TColumn> {
120	  const columnsWithError = columns.filter((column) =>
121	    columnHasBoundError(column, errors, match),
122	  );
123	  const unmatchedFieldKeys = unmatchedRowErrorFieldKeys(columns, errors, match);
124	  return {
125	    hasError: columnsWithError.length > 0 || unmatchedFieldKeys.length > 0,
126	    unmatchedFieldKeys,
127	    mobileHiddenErrorColumns: columnsWithError.filter(
128	      (column) => column.mobileHidden,
129	    ),
